name: Blockchain
description: Blockchains from hash chains and signatures up: consensus, Bitcoin and Ethereum, smart contracts and scaling.

nodes.name: Blockchain basics
nodes.desc: Blocks, hash pointers, ledgers and what problem blockchains solve.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how blocks linked by hash pointers form a tamper-evident ledger and what problem blockchains solve.
topics: Distributed ledgers without a central party

nodes.name: Merkle trees
nodes.desc: Merkle trees, inclusion proofs and light clients.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build a Merkle tree, verify inclusion proofs and explain how light clients rely on them.
topics: Building a Merkle tree from transactions
Inclusion proofs of log n size

nodes.name: Keys & wallets
nodes.desc: Key pairs, addresses, signatures and wallet types.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how key pairs, addresses and digital signatures work and compare wallet types.
topics: Hierarchical deterministic wallets and seed phrases

nodes.name: Peer-to-peer network
nodes.desc: Gossip, node discovery and propagating blocks and transactions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe how blockchain nodes discover peers and propagate transactions and blocks over a gossip network.

nodes.name: UTXO transactions
nodes.desc: Bitcoin's UTXO model, transaction structure and scripts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read Bitcoin transactions in the UTXO model and explain how inputs, outputs and scripts authorise spending.

nodes.name: Proof of work
nodes.desc: Mining, difficulty, the longest-chain rule and 51% attacks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain proof-of-work mining, difficulty adjustment, the longest-chain rule and the risk of 51% attacks.

nodes.name: Proof of stake
nodes.desc: Staking, validators, slashing and finality gadgets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how proof-of-stake chains select validators, punish misbehaviour with slashing and reach finality.

nodes.name: BFT consensus
nodes.desc: Byzantine fault tolerant protocols used by permissioned and PoS chains.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe Byzantine fault tolerant consensus protocols and their 3f+1 fault bound as used by permissioned and PoS chains.

nodes.name: Forks & finality
nodes.desc: Soft and hard forks, reorgs and probabilistic vs absolute finality.
nodes.summary: You will be able to distinguish soft and hard forks, explain chain reorganisations and compare probabilistic and absolute finality.

nodes.name: Ethereum & the EVM
nodes.desc: Accounts, gas and the Ethereum Virtual Machine.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain Ethereum accounts, gas and how the EVM executes contract code.

nodes.name: Solidity basics
nodes.desc: Writing, testing and deploying smart contracts in Solidity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write, test and deploy Solidity smart contracts with state, functions, events and modifiers.

nodes.name: Contract security
nodes.desc: Reentrancy, overflow, front-running and auditing practices.
nodes.summary: You will be able to spot common smart contract vulnerabilities such as reentrancy and front-running and apply auditing practices.

nodes.name: Tokens & NFTs
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain fungible and non-fungible token standards and the functions and events they require.

nodes.name: Token project
nodes.desc: Write, test and deploy your own token contract to a test network.
nodes.summary: You will write, test and deploy your own token contract to a test network and interact with it from a wallet.

nodes.name: Layer 2 scaling
nodes.desc: Payment channels, optimistic and zk rollups.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how payment channels and optimistic and zk rollups scale blockchains while inheriting layer 1 security.

nodes.name: DeFi
nodes.desc: Exchanges, lending and stablecoins built from contracts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how decentralised exchanges, lending protocols and stablecoins are built from smart contracts.

nodes.name: dApp frontends
nodes.desc: Connecting a web frontend to contracts and wallets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to connect a web frontend to smart contracts and user wallets to read state and send transactions.

nodes.name: Privacy & ZK
nodes.desc: Privacy coins and zero-knowledge proofs on chain.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how privacy coins and zero-knowledge proofs hide transaction details while keeping them verifiable.
topics: Privacy coins like Zcash and Monero

nodes.name: dApp project
nodes.desc: Build a full dApp: contract, tests and a web frontend on a test network.
nodes.summary: You will build a complete dApp with a tested smart contract and a web frontend deployed on a test network.
